messages.subject: Multiple imputation question
parts:
Greetings,

I'm estimating a simple path model that works using FIML for missing data, but when I run the following line

fitmi <- runMI(pathmodel, data=scimodel,m=5,seed=12345, miPackage="Amelia", fun="sem",chi="all")

I receive 10 warnings that all say 

In estimateVCOV(lavaanModel, samplestats = lavaanSampleStats, options = lavaanOptions,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!

Yet, I receive output that looks fine. 

lavaan (0.5-15) converged normally after   5 iterations

  Number of observations                          7361

  Estimator                                         ML
  Minimum Function Test Statistic              783.275
  Degrees of freedom                                10
  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.000

Parameter estimates:

  Information                                 Expected
  Standard Errors                             Standard

                   Estimate  Std.err  Z-value  P(>|z|)
Regressions:
  sciach ~
    scigrade10        0.870    0.032   27.448    0.000
  scigrade10 ~
    scigrade6         0.805    0.020   40.113    0.000
    ses               0.166    0.032    5.217    0.000
    certsci          -0.043    0.039   -1.095    0.274
    understand        0.169    0.015   11.325    0.000
    challenge        -0.031    0.017   -1.821    0.069
  challenge ~
    understand        0.318    0.010   33.225    0.000
  understand ~
    certsci          -0.030    0.033   -0.929    0.353

Variances:
    sciach           22.379    0.380
    scigrade10        2.656    0.044
    challenge         1.250    0.021
    understand        1.858    0.031


Notice that standard errors are computed and look roughly similar to FIML.

But, I do not receive all the chi-squares when asking for chi="all".  I did try inspect(fitmi, "fit"), but that didn't produce the chi-squares.

Thoughts?

Thanks.

David

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Multiple imputation question
parts:
Hi David

This could be for a characteristic of the Menag and Rubin method to combine the chi-square (also used by mplus).

This method has several steps, and there is one step that is more propense to create problems. Since the chi-square is not related to the parameters, you will get parameters, but no fit indices.

If you set chi="lmrr" you will get fit indices based in another method to combine the chi-square.

What I recommend whe using MI is to create the imputations outside of the runMI function, and give the list object with the imputations to runMI. Doing it this way alow you to check and diagnose the imputations.

For the imputations you shoudl check if your data is multivariate normal to the use of Amelia, if not I would recommend to use mice, for mice you have to make sure to use the right method of imputation, and check the convergence, mice doesnt have a convergence criteria, you have to review that, if not you have to increase the iterations

bye
